data.title: Leapmotor's Shares Sharply Lower After Third-Quarter Profitability Weakness
data.description:
By Jiahui Huang

Shares of Zhejiang Leapmotor Technology fell sharply, after the Chinese automaker's gross profit margin declined in the third quarter.

Its shares dropped 14% to 26.18 Hong Kong dollars early Monday, sharper than the benchmark Hang Seng Index's 0.5% fall.

Leapmotor's decline came after the automaker said its gross profit margin fell to 10.9% in the third quarter, compared with 12.6% in the second quarter and 14.5% a year earlier. Higher material and freight costs weighed on profitability.

Jefferies analysts expect a modest recovery in the company's gross profit margin in the fourth quarter, as memory-chip prices remain high, they said in a note.

Leapmotor's third-quarter revenue rose 63% to 31.7 billion yuan, equivalent to $4.75 billion. However, its net profit plunged to 40 million yuan from 150 million yuan a year earlier despite a record delivery volume of 310,052 units during the period. The company attributed its lower net profit to weaker profitability per vehicle.

Like many of its Chinese peers, Leapmotor faces subdued domestic demand. Sales in foreign markets could offset weakness at home, Jefferies analysts said, adding that the company's overseas profitability could strengthen next year.

The company's vehicle production in overseas markets will likely give it an upper hand in hedging against tariff risks compared with its Chinese peers, they added.

data.title: EU Inks Deals With Indonesia to Cut Tariffs, Catalyze Investment
data.description:
By Ying Xian Wong and Fabiana Negrin Ochoa

The European Union signed ambitious agreements with Indonesia that eliminate most tariffs on goods between the two sides, aiming to will deliver billions in economic benefits.

Brussels announced the Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement with Indonesia on Saturday, more than 10 years after negotiations began. The parties also inked an Investment Protection Agreement to encourage bilateral flows.

"EU-Indonesia trade and investment has vast untapped potential," said Ursula von der Leyen, president of the European Commission.

Duties on main EU export products, including meat and dairy, will be removed, while existing tariffs on cars, machinery, chemicals and pharmaceuticals will be cut.

According to Indonesia's Coordinating Ministry for Economic Affairs, about 90% of tariffs on EU-bound exports to the EU will be removed, while others will be gradually reduced over 3 to 15 years or benefit from tariff-rate quotas.

The preferential access is expected to make Indonesian exports--particularly footwear, textiles and processed commodities--more competitive in the European market, it added.

The pacts open "new doors for businesses," bolstering cooperation in sectors like agri-food and advanced manufacturing, said EU Commissioner for Trade and Economic Security Maroš Šefčovič.

With the deals in place, EU shipments to Indonesia are projected to increase by nearly 40% over 15 years, while Indonesian exports of goods and services to the bloc are expected to rise by more than 14%.

"This will boost economic growth," the commission said, projecting that the EU's gross domestic product will be 16 billion euros higher and Indonesia's 27 billion euros higher, or $17.55 billion and $29.62 billion respectively.

Lowered trade barriers and streamlined investment frameworks will unlock opportunities for European businesses and farmers in Indonesia's market of 280 million consumers, the commission said. EU exporters stand to save over $650 million in annual duties.

Another key benefit for the EU is access to Indonesia's vast resources of materials like nickel and cobalt that are used in everything from electric vehicles to jet engines.

The agreement will give manufacturers stable, predictable access to critical resources, strengthening the trading bloc's supply chain against shocks, the commission said.

"It also provides an export duty-free quota for crude palm and palm kernel oil, both of which are strategic inputs for EU industries," it added.

Recent supply-chain disruptions stemming from wars and other shocks have underlined the need for countries to build up resilience via trade alliances and diversification.

The EU has already concluded agreements with Singapore and Vietnam, and is in ongoing trade negotiations with Thailand and the Philippines.

The investment and economic partnerships struck with Indonesia require the European Parliament's consent and Indonesia's internal ratification. They are expected to be provisionally applied in early 2027.

data.title: ModelBest opening up access to AI technology on an international scale
data.description:
ModelBest opening up access to AI technology on an international scale

ModelBest opening up access to AI technology on an international scale

PR Newswire

LISBON, Portugal, Nov. 22, 2026

LISBON, Portugal, Nov. 22, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- This is a report from China Daily:

The global race for artificial intelligence is often perceived as a competition over who controls the largest data centers. However, ModelBest offers a different perspective: how inclusive intelligence becomes depends on its accessibility and how widely it can be deployed.

This Chinese on-device AI unicorn has made efficiency the cornerstone of its overseas expansion strategy. By November, its self-developed MiniCPM series of models had recorded more than 70 million downloads worldwide.

"MiniCPM is not just one model. It is an entire family," Li Dahai, CEO of ModelBest, said at the Web Summit 2026 in Lisbon, Portugal, which took place from Nov 9 to 12.

Each model serves a different form of intelligence, but they share one goal: higher intelligence density, faster speed, and lower cost on devices, he added.

That efficiency-first approach has been put to work abroad. In April, ModelBest revealed the Lao national model, LaoAI, which marked a landmark case of a Chinese AI company helping another nation build its own national AI foundation.

Built on the company's MiniCPM architecture and high-efficiency training methods, the system is integrated into G-Chat v2, the national government communications platform, and is used across government agencies and key industries.

Sovereign AI has largely been dominated by chipmakers, for whom sovereignty implies acquiring advanced computing power and constructing national data centers. LaoAI offers another path: instead of relying on a national supercomputing cluster, the team made multiple field research trips to Laos in the months leading up to the launch, building the system on high-efficiency model architecture rather than massive computing power.

The team also incorporated Lao culture and values into training through field research. The Lao translation capability of their model outperforms mainstream systems on international benchmarks.

Crucially, the underlying model and application programming interfaces are open to local developers. The complete model weights have been delivered to the Lao side, giving them control over everything from the model to the data.

"Efficiency is the key to making large model technology available to everyone," Li said. "In the Lao national model project, an 8-billion-parameter system achieved world-leading Lao-language capability. This demonstrates that developing countries need not wait for top-tier computing power to benefit from AI," he added.

The significance is more developmental than commercial: countries of the Global South no longer need access to high-end computing capacity to step into the AI era.

The same principle applies to businesses. Making AI affordable for small and medium-sized enterprises is often touted but rarely realized. ModelBest's on-device approach changes that. When inference happens on the device, small businesses need neither cloud capacity nor data uploads to access usable AI.

The technical foundation is what the company calls the "Densing Law". The capability density of large models doubles roughly every 3.5 months, reducing the number of parameters needed for a given level of intelligence.

For such businesses, on-device AI is not merely cheaper: it is their first realistic chance to possess AI capability, with data on-premises, no per-inference fees, and no dependence on network coverage.

From sovereign models to on-device intelligence, ModelBest's international narrative aims to share the benefits of China's AI advancements with more countries, ensuring that each nation can develop its own AI capabilities in its own languages.

This direction echoes national policy: China's 2026 Government Work Report endorsed open-source AI ecosystems, and this year's World Artificial Intelligence Conference and the World Internet Conference Wuzhen Summit both advanced initiatives for a fair, open and sustainable global AI ecosystem.

For ModelBest, the overseas initiatives represent a microcosm of this broader vision. By prioritizing efficiency and openness, AI can be extended to countries and businesses that have been waiting on the sidelines.

Beyond expanding access, ModelBest is also rethinking how AI itself is built. The next step is to use AI to build AI itself.

"This is not only a technological change; it is a fundamental shift in how intelligence is produced," Li said.

data.title: DBS Raises Over $155 Million By Opening Wealth Strategy to Retail Investors
data.description:
By P.R. Venkat

DBS has raised more than US$155 million from retail investors through a fund based on a strategy previously available only to its wealth clients.

The multiasset DBS Chief Investment Office Barbell Strategy Fund, which raised 200 million Singapore dollars from the new group of investors, is actively managed through market cycles. The strategy it follows has delivered an annualized net return of 7.9% since its inception in 2019, DBS said Monday.

"With this fund, we are extending a flagship strategy previously available only to our wealth clients to a wider group of investors. As market volatility becomes the new norm, we hope to enable our customers to invest consistently with greater confidence as they grow their wealth," DBS Head of Investment Products (Consumer Banking Group) Chua Yi Wen said.

The DBS CIO Barbell Strategy Fund invests in fast-growing stocks in areas such as artificial intelligence, semiconductors and cloud computing, alongside global bonds and alternatives such as gold and hedge funds.
